mainTopic: The sixteenth case of a woman who exempts her צרה, and the מחלוקת between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן over כרת for a חלוצה and her צרה
overview: The גמרא finishes a special case: a man's mother, raped by his father, later marries his paternal brother. When that brother dies childless, she exempts her צרה from the son, so this is added as a sixteenth case to the משנה's fifteen. ריש לקיש asks why the משנה does not also list a man who did חליצה, then betrothed the same woman and died. רבי יוחנן answers that this case cannot produce a צרת צרה, and the גמרא explains he was answering on ריש לקיש's terms, since in his own view a חלוצה is only a לאו. The גמרא then quotes their full מחלוקת. ריש לקיש says the חולץ has only a לאו with the חלוצה, while the other brothers, and everyone with the צרה, get כרת. He learns this from the פסוק "אשר לא יבנה". רבי יוחנן says no one gets כרת, because one חליצה acts for all the brothers and all the wives. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא, ריש לקיש answers from its ending, and רב ששת splits the ברייתא between the רבנן and רבי עקיבא. The amud ends by asking why the ברייתא did not name רבי עקיבא, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case of a mother raped by the father who marries the paternal brother
steps.stepSummary: A man's mother, who was raped by his father, marries his paternal brother. When that brother dies, she exempts her צרה from יבום with the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his mother was a woman his father had raped, and she later married his brother from the same father, and that brother died, this is a case of 'his mother' who exempts her rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing a case where a man's own mother falls to him for יבום and so exempts her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man's mother cannot fall to him for יבום, because she would have to be married to his brother, who is also her son or her husband's son. Here the father only raped her and never married her, so she was able to marry the father's other son. When that brother dies childless, she and her צרה both come before the son. Since the mother is an ערוה to him, her צרה is exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman his father raped (not married)
His brother from the same father
Her rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
Exempts (from יבום and חליצה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the brothers. The son here is a different son from the brother she married. Both brothers share a father, but the mother here is the son's own mother.

phrases.english: If his mother was a woman raped by his father,
and she married his brother from his father,
and he (that brother) died,
this is the case of his mother who exempts her rival wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about how 'his mother' could exempt a צרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mother raped by the father who married his paternal brother, and was widowed childless, exempts her צרה from the son.

steps.title: Adding a sixteenth case to the list
steps.stepSummary: The משנה counts fifteen women who exempt their rival wives, but this case must be added as a sixteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the Sages taught 'fifteen' in our משנה, we must add a sixteenth case like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The statement ends by concluding that the משנה's list of fifteen needs a sixteenth case, the mother case from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a fixed number, fifteen, which sounds like a complete list. This statement says the number is not complete, because the mother case also works. That raises the question of what kinds of cases the משנה's list includes, which ריש לקיש asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fifteen (the משנה's count of women who exempt their צרות)
To add
Like this one

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's count of fifteen is not a closed list. The mother-raped-by-father case becomes a sixteenth.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once a sixteenth case is added, the obvious question is which other cases could be added too. The rest of this section deals with that question.

phrases.english: And even though the Sages taught
in our Mishnah "fifteen,"

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָנוּ לְהוֹסִיף שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה כְּגוֹן זוֹ.
phrases.english: we have to add a sixteenth, like this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ ״חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the case in Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sixteenth case, the mother raped by the father, must be added to the משנה's fifteen.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks why the חולץ who remarried is not listed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש argues that according to לוי, the משנה should also list a man who did חליצה with his יבמה, then betrothed her and died childless.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: According to לוי, who says the משנה also teaches cases that only happen through a forbidden act, let it also teach the case of a man who did חליצה with his יבמה, then went back and betrothed her, and died without children. Since she is forbidden, her rival wife should be forbidden too!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן. If the משנה includes cases that only arise through a forbidden act, it should also include the case of the חלוצה who was betrothed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי holds that the משנה also teaches 'what if' cases, meaning situations that only happen if someone does something forbidden. Marrying your own חלוצה is forbidden, but if it happens and the man dies, she is forbidden to his brothers. So ריש לקיש argues that she should exempt her צרה and be listed too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What if' cases, which only arise if someone does a forbidden act
One who does חליצה with his יבמה
And then went back and betrothed her
Since (because of one fact, another follows)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
According to Levi, who said it also teaches "what if" cases,
phrases.notes: These are cases that only happen if someone breaks a rule, like the father in Step 1.

phrases.english: let it teach: one who does חליצה with his יבמה
and then went back and betrothed her,
and died without children,
since she herself is forbidden,
her rival wife is forbidden too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְלֵוִי דַּאֲמַר ״דְּאִי״ נָמֵי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the addition of a sixteenth case and asks why another 'what if' case was not also added.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that the משנה includes 'what if' cases, together with the decision to add only a sixteenth case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If forbidden-act cases count, the חולץ who remarried his חלוצה also produces a forbidden woman whose צרה should be forbidden, so it should be listed too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: this case has no rival of a rival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the חולץ case is left out because it cannot produce a צרת צרה, unlike the cases in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because this case does not work as a 'rival of a rival.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends the list. The חולץ case is left out because it cannot reach the further stage of a rival wife's rival wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case in the משנה works not only for the צרה but also for the צרה of the צרה. In the חולץ case, the חליצה makes the woman forbidden to all the brothers equally, so none of them can marry her צרה and create another rival. Because that part of the pattern is missing, the case does not fit the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: The rival wife of a rival wife
Because

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Yochanan) said to him:
Because it does not work as a rival of a rival.
phrases.notes: All the משנה's cases go on to the rival's rival as well. This one stops after the first rival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּצָרַת צָרָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: it lacks a feature that all the listed cases share.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any case where the woman is forbidden and so forbids her צרה belongs in the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only cases that also work for a צרת צרה are listed, and the חולץ case does not.

steps.title: Why not answer that a חלוצה is only a לאו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not give a simpler answer: a חלוצה is forbidden only by a לאו, and such women are still subject to חליצה and יבום, so her צרה is not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to him: She is a woman forbidden only by a negative commandment, and women forbidden by a negative commandment are still subject to חליצה and יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's answer and suggests a simpler one he could have given. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's fifteen women are all ערוות forbidden with כרת, and only that kind of ban fully exempts a צרה. A חלוצה is forbidden only by a לאו, and a woman under a לאו still falls under חליצה and יבום. So her צרה should not be exempt at all, which seems an easier reason to leave the case out.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden by a regular negative commandment (not כרת)
Still subject to חליצה and יבום
But let him say to him (why not answer this way?)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יוחנן was wrong. It is asking why he picked his answer over a simpler one.

phrases.english: But let him (Rabbi Yochanan) say to him:
she is among those forbidden by a negative commandment,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין בְּנֵי חֲלִיצָה וְיִבּוּם נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: and those forbidden by a negative commandment are subject to חליצה and יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 4 by suggesting a simpler one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's choice of the 'no rival of a rival' answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חלוצה is forbidden only by a לאו, so she still falls under חליצה and יבום and cannot exempt her צרה. That is a simpler reason to leave the case out of the משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answered according to ריש לקיש's own view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן did not use the simpler answer because he was answering inside ריש לקיש's view. In that view the brothers get כרת for a חלוצה, so he needed the צרת צרה answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was answering him on his own terms. In my view, these women are only forbidden by a לאו, and women forbidden by a לאו still go through חליצה and יבום. But in your view, they carry כרת. So I had to answer: the case is left out because it cannot produce a צרת צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. It explains why רבי יוחנן gave the צרת צרה answer instead of the simpler "it's only a לאו" answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן personally holds that a חלוצה is only a לאו, so the case never belonged in the משנה at all. ריש לקיש, though, holds the other brothers get כרת for her, which would make her like the women in the משנה. So רבי יוחנן answered ריש לקיש with a reason that works even in ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his (the other person's) words or view
According to me / according to you
Women forbidden by an ordinary negative commandment (no כרת)
Women forbidden with the punishment of כרת
The rival wife of a rival wife

steps.confusionAlert: "לדידי" here is רבי יוחנן speaking about his own view, and "לדידך" is ריש לקיש's view. רבי יוחנן's answer about צרת צרה was not his main reason. It was a reason that works even for ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: He was speaking to him according to his words:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering ריש לקיש using ריש לקיש's own opinion, not his own.

phrases.english: According to me, they are ones forbidden by a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין בְּנֵי חֲלִיצָה וְיִבּוּם נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: and those forbidden by a prohibition are subject to חליצה and יבום.
But according to you, they are ones liable to כרת.
So the reason is that they do not have a rival of a rival.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer given according to the other side's view (לדבריו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן should have said a חלוצה is only a לאו, so her צרה is not exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is רבי יוחנן's own view. For ריש לקיש, who holds the brothers get כרת, the only answer that works is the lack of a צרת צרה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's own view: a חלוצה is only a לאו. ריש לקיש's view: the brothers get כרת for her. The צרת צרה answer was given on ריש לקיש's terms.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view on one who did חליצה and then betrothed her
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a man did חליצה with his יבמה and then betrothed her. ריש לקיש says he gets no כרת for her, but the other brothers do. For the צרה, everyone gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a man did חליצה with his יבמה and then went back and betrothed her. ריש לקיש said: he himself is not liable to כרת for the חלוצה, but the other brothers are. As for the rival wife, both he and the brothers are liable to כרת for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the full מחלוקת that the earlier discussion hinted at. This step gives ריש לקיש's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש splits the cases. The brother who actually did the חליצה is not liable to כרת for the חלוצה. The other brothers still get כרת for her as a brother's wife. The צרה, who did not do the חליצה herself, carries כרת for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated": it introduces a מחלוקת between אמוראים
The brother who performs חליצה
The woman who went through חליצה
Spiritual cutting off: the punishment for forbidden relations like a brother's wife

phrases.english: It was stated: One who does חליצה with his יבמה
and then went back and betrothed her,
Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא — אֵין חַיָּיב עַל הַחֲלוּצָה כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: He is not liable to כרת for the חלוצה,
but the brothers are liable to כרת for the חלוצה.
As for the rival wife,
both he and the brothers
are liable to כרת for the rival wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the מחלוקת that step 6 relied on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brother who did חליצה gets no כרת for the חלוצה. The other brothers get כרת for her. Everyone gets כרת for the צרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's view: no כרת for anyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says neither the brother who did חליצה nor the other brothers get כרת, whether for the חלוצה or for the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: neither he nor the brothers are liable to כרת, not for the חלוצה and not for the rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the חליצה fully removes the brother's-wife prohibition from both women and for all the brothers. So no one is left with a כרת prohibition. This matches what he said in step 6, that these are only לאוין.

keyTerms.meaning: Both he (the one who did חליצה) and the other brothers
They are not liable
Neither... nor...

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says there is כרת for the other brothers and for the צרה. רבי יוחנן says there is no כרת at all for anyone.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הוּא וּבֵין הָאַחִין אֵינָן חַיָּיבִין
phrases.english: Both he and the brothers are not liable
to כרת, neither for the חלוצה
nor to כרת for the rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בֵּין הוּא וּבֵין הָאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to ריש לקיש in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one gets כרת, whether for the חלוצה or for the צרה.

steps.title: What is ריש לקיש's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of ריש לקיש's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש rules as he does. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's ruling treats the brother who did חליצה differently from everyone else. That needs a source, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Reish Lakish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for ריש לקיש's ruling

steps.title: The פסוק "אשר לא יבנה": once he didn't build, he may never build
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from "אשר לא יבנה" that once the brother chose חליצה instead of building his brother's house, he may never build it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "who will not build." Since he did not build, he shall not build again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's source: the words "אשר לא יבנה" from the חליצה section of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "לא יבנה" are read as a rule, not just a description: after חליצה he may not go back and marry her. This prohibition is aimed at the brother who did the חליצה, which helps explain why ריש לקיש treats him differently from the other brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק says": it introduces a source from the תורה
"Who will not build" (his brother's house)
He shall not build again

phrases.english: The verse states: "Who will not build,"

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא בָּנָה — שׁוּב לֹא יִבְנֶה.
phrases.english: once he did not build, he shall not build again.
phrases.notes: "Build" means marrying her through יבום. He chose חליצה instead, so now he can't marry her.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "אשר לא יבנה" teaches that after חליצה the brother may never do יבום with her. This is a prohibition directed at him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the basis for ריש לקיש treating the brother who did חליצה (a לאו only) differently from the other brothers (כרת).

steps.title: Only the brother who did חליצה is under 'לא יבנה'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's derivation applies only to the חולץ himself. The other brothers stay with the original כרת prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only he who stands under 'does not build.' But his brothers stay exactly where they stood before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues ריש לקיש's answer from the פסוק. It explains why the brothers still get כרת for the חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר לא יבנה' speak about the one who refused to build, which is the brother who did חליצה. So only his prohibition becomes the lighter לאו of 'לא יבנה.' The other brothers never did anything, so for them she goes back to plain אשת אח, which carries כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Does not build', the pasuk about the brother who refuses יבום
They stay where they stood (their status is unchanged)
His brothers, the other יבמים

phrases.english: It is he who stands under "does not build,"
but his brothers — as they stood, they stand.
phrases.notes: Before the brother died she was their brother's wife, which carries כרת. That is where they return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the derivation from step 10 by limiting it to the brother who did חליצה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק speaks only of the חולץ, so the brothers keep the original כרת prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חולץ gets a לאו. The other brothers get כרת for the חלוצה.

steps.title: 'לא יבנה' covers only the חלוצה, not her צרה
steps.stepSummary: Even for the חולץ, the lighter status applies only to the woman he did חליצה with. Her צרה stays under כרת for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is only regarding her that he stands under 'does not build.' But the צרה stays exactly where she stood before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit to ריש לקיש's reading. It explains why everyone, even the חולץ, gets כרת for the צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חולץ refused to build only with the woman he did חליצה with. The צרה was not part of that act, so 'לא יבנה' does not touch her. She returns to the original כרת prohibition of אשת אח for all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: The co-wife of the יבמה
Regarding her herself (the חלוצה)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: 'לא יבנה' changes only the חולץ, and only with the חלוצה. In every other combination there is כרת.

phrases.english: And regarding her herself,
he stands under "does not build,"
but the rival wife — as she stood, she stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲלֵהּ דִּידַהּ, הוּא דְּקָאֵי בְּ״לֹא יִבְנֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the derivation. Step 11 limited which man is affected, and this step limits which woman is affected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא יבנה' applies only to the חלוצה herself, so the צרה stays under כרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, including the חולץ, gets כרת for the צרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the כרת prohibition cannot come back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues that before the חליצה every brother could do חליצה with every wife. So it makes no sense that כרת suddenly returns afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: Is there such a thing? At the start, if this brother wanted, he could do חליצה, and if that brother wanted, he could do חליצה. If he wanted, he could do חליצה with this wife, and if he wanted, with that wife. And now someone would get כרת for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי יוחנן's reasoning. He uses a rhetorical question to show that ריש לקיש's idea does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the brother died, the אשת אח prohibition was set aside for all the brothers and all the wives, because any of them could be part of the יבום or חליצה. Something that was fully set aside cannot simply return with כרת because one pair did חליצה. This attacks the idea that the others go back to how 'they stood before.'

keyTerms.meaning: Is there such a thing? (a rhetorical challenge)
At the start, before the חליצה
Does חליצה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Is there such a thing
that at the outset, if this one wanted, he could do חליצה,
and if that one wanted, he could do חליצה,
and if he wanted, he could do חליצה with this one,
and if he wanted, he could do חליצה with that one,
and now he stands to get כרת for her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from ריש לקיש's reasoning to רבי יוחנן's, beginning by rejecting the idea that the old prohibition returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the other brothers and the צרה return to their original כרת status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשת אח prohibition was set aside for every brother and every wife when the brother died, so it cannot come back with כרת after the חליצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one gets כרת after the חליצה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן's reason begins with this point: the אשת אח prohibition was set aside for every brother and every wife at the outset, so כרת cannot come back after one חליצה.

steps.title: The חולץ acts for all the brothers, and she acts for her צרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that one חליצה works for everyone. The brother acts as the agent of the other brothers, and the woman acts as the agent of her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is doing the agency of the brothers, and she is doing the agency of the צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the positive reason for his view. One חליצה counts as if all the brothers released all the wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חולץ is not acting alone. He acts for all the brothers, so all of them are in the same position he is. Likewise, the חלוצה's act also covers the צרה. So nobody 'stays as he stood,' and there is no כרת for anyone, just as רבי יוחנן said in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Agency, acting on someone else's behalf
He is doing

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: only the חולץ with the חלוצה is changed, and every other combination has כרת. רבי יוחנן: one חליצה acts for all the brothers and all the wives, so there is no כרת for anyone.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real שליחות where the brothers appointed him. It means his חליצה automatically counts for all of them.

phrases.english: Rather, he is performing the agency of the brothers,
she is performing the agency of the rival wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting ריש לקיש's logic in step 13, רבי יוחנן gives his own reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חליצה of one brother and one wife counts for all the brothers and all the wives, so there is no כרת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבי יוחנן's view, one חליצה releases the whole family, so the brothers and the צרה are under the same lighter status and none of them gets כרת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a remarried חלוצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא: a man did חליצה with his יבמה, remarried her, then died. She needs חליצה from the brothers. That fits a לאו, not כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from a ברייתא. A man did חליצה with his יבמה, later betrothed her, and then died. She needs חליצה from the other brothers. This works for me, since I say the brothers have only a regular לאו with her. That is why she needs חליצה. But according to you, why would she need חליצה at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא and argues that it works only with his view, not with ריש לקיש's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband dies, she comes before the other brothers again. If the brothers are forbidden to her by a regular לאו (רבי יוחנן), she still needs חליצה, just not יבום. If they are forbidden by כרת (ריש לקיש), she should be completely free from them, with no חליצה needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
The brother who did חליצה with his brother's widow
People forbidden by a regular prohibition, not כרת
It makes sense / it works well (according to one view)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the remarriage by the חולץ himself works, since for him even ריש לקיש says there is no כרת, only the לאו of 'לא יבנה' (steps 7 and 10–11). The fight is about the other brothers after he dies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
One who did chalitza with his yevama,
and then went back and betrothed her, and died
she needs chalitza from the brothers.
This works well according to me,
since I say they are liable only for a regular prohibition,
phrases.notes: "They" means the other brothers, if they would marry this חלוצה.

phrases.english: that is why she needs chalitza from the brothers.
But according to you,
why does she need chalitza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views were explained, רבי יוחנן now attacks ריש לקיש's view directly from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the brothers are under כרת with the חלוצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman forbidden by כרת needs no חליצה. The ברייתא requires חליצה, so the prohibition must be only a לאו.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers from the end of the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש points to the last part: if a brother betrothed her, it does not take effect at all. That fits כרת, not a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, look at the last part: if one of the brothers betrothed her, she has no claim on him at all. If the brothers have only a regular לאו, why does the betrothal not work?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש turns the same ברייתא back on רבי יוחנן, showing that its ending fits only the כרת view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a betrothal still takes effect even when there is only a לאו. Saying the betrothal is worth nothing means it is a כרת case. So the ברייתא seems to argue with itself, and רבי יוחנן cannot fully rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: turning the question back on the asker
The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
She has no claim on him at all; the betrothal did not take effect

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the last part:
If one of the brothers got up and betrothed her,
she has nothing on him.
phrases.notes: Meaning the betrothal didn't take hold, so she doesn't even need a גט from him.

phrases.english: But if they are liable only for a regular prohibition,
why does she have nothing on him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge with a counter-challenge from the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the brothers have only a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Betrothal works with a לאו but not with כרת. The ברייתא says a brother's betrothal does not work, which fits only כרת.

steps.title: רב ששת: the last part follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the last part of the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that betrothal does not take effect even with a regular לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: the last part follows רבי עקיבא, who said that betrothal does not take effect with people forbidden by a regular לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends רבי יוחנן by saying the two parts of the ברייתא follow different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, even a regular לאו is enough to stop a betrothal. So the last part can be a לאו case and still say the betrothal is worthless. The first part follows the רבנן, and רבי יוחנן's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (another opinion): this part follows a different תנא
Betrothal does not take hold

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
In the last part, we have come to Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין קִידּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בְּחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין.
phrases.english: who said: betrothal does not take hold with those forbidden by a regular prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves ריש לקיש's counter-challenge in favor of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: the first part follows the רבנן, the last part follows רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last part says betrothal fails, so it must be a כרת case.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, betrothal fails even with a לאו, so the last part does not prove כרת.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have named רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the last part follows רבי עקיבא, the ברייתא should have said 'according to רבי עקיבא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let it teach: according to רבי עקיבא, she has no claim on him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer: a ברייתא that switches opinions usually says so openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the wording shows a switch to a different תנא. If the last part really followed רבי עקיבא, we would expect his name there. So רב ששת's split looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach: the text should have said it this way
According to the words of

phrases.english: But then let it teach:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֵין לוֹ עָלָיו כְּלוּם!
phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Akiva, she has nothing on him!
phrases.notes: The text says לו (him), but it means the same as לה (her) in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the last part follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא changed to a different opinion, it should have named רבי עקיבא. Since it didn't, the split is hard to accept.
